title: Listen at the four heart sites on a manikin with a stethoscope: diaphragm flat, sealed and still at each, in order
keywords: flat contact on a curved surface
instruction: Listen to the manikin's heart with the stethoscope at the aortic, pulmonic, tricuspid and mitral areas, in that order, holding it on each for 2 seconds, then put the chestpiece back in its tray.
context: Registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141.00, 3.47 million US jobs: "Monitor, record, and report symptoms or changes in patients' conditions") and LPNs (29-2061.00, 0.67 million) listen to hearts in routine assessments. Open RN Nursing Skills: "The aortic area is the second intercostal space to the right of the sternum ... Auscultation usually begins at the aortic area ... Move the stethoscope sequentially to the pulmonic area". The 43 mm diaphragm hears only with its whole rim on the skin, pressed firmly. The chest is curved, so the slope under the disc changes at each site (head-to-foot 9.7 deg at the 2nd rib spaces, 4.4 deg at the 4th; left-right 5 deg at the sternum's edges, 26 deg at the mitral area): the rim seals only with the disc within about 2 deg of the skin and pressed 2-10 N, held still 2 s. The soft arm sets the press by how far past the skin it aims, and an off-centre press tips the disc off.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. (1) Adult chest trainer (a manikin torso), fixed, lying on its back across the table, head toward +y, its right side toward the robot: a torso from the neck to the upper abdomen, 32 cm wide (x 4 to 36; 38 cm at the shoulders), 21.5 cm deep at the 4th-5th ribs, 19.3 cm at the sternal notch, from y -17.5 to 11.5 plus a neck stub; firm vinyl skin. Midline at x 20.0, sternal notch at y 6.5. Sites (x, y, height): aortic (17.2, 0.5, 20.5), pulmonic (22.8, 0.5, 20.5), tricuspid (22.8, -5.0, 21.2), mitral (29.5, -7.5, 19.6). (2) Stethoscope chestpiece (Littmann Classic III type), loose, 80 g: steel two-sided head 44.5 mm across, 22 mm tall, adult diaphragm 43 mm in a rubber rim; 8 mm stem 62 mm long from the head's axis. It lies diaphragm down in (3) a steel tray, fixed, 13 x 10 cm inside, 1.5 cm walls, centred at (22.5, -25.5); head at (19.5, -25.5), stem toward +x. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every 50 ms step: the rim's pose, the rim's contact force on the torso (PhysX pair force) and the fingers' collision points. A site is heard when, for 2 s in a row, all 24 points round the 43 mm rim are within 0.5 mm of the skin or pressed into it, the force is 2-10 N, the disc's centre is within 20 mm of the site (along the skin) and moves under 3 mm. Sites count only in order: aortic, pulmonic, tricuspid, mitral. 0.2 per site heard. 1.0 (held 1 s): all four heard and the chestpiece lying in its tray (face within 4 mm of the floor, tilted under 10 deg), every finger point 2 cm or more from it, still (under 1 mm in 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the trainer lies on a tared kitchen scale filmed with the run, and the rim is inked with washable stamp ink; a site counts when the video shows the chestpiece resting there for 2 s with the scale at 204-1020 g (2-10 N) and the photo afterwards shows there a complete, unsmeared ring whose centre is inside the site's 20 mm circle on a clear overlay laid on the trainer by its notch and midline marks; in order and the end state from the video.
reset_notes: Wipe the ink rings off the trainer with an alcohol wipe, re-ink the diaphragm's rim on the stamp pad (one press), lay the chestpiece diaphragm down in its tray, head at the marked spot and stem toward the far side, and tare the scale. In simulation each trial starts afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz. The trainer's skin and the rubber rim give as one compliant contact on the rim (1.2 N/mm per contact point; the face sinks about 1.3 mm at 4.5 N); the seal is judged from the rim's 24 points, not from sound. The torso is built from measured cross-sections, not a scan, with smooth skin (ribs not shaped). The tubing and earpieces are not simulated; the head sits on the stem rigidly.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (the right arm reached over the chest early on, then went down to the chestpiece in its tray and hovered at it without taking it; no site was heard); demo: 1.0
